clash-in-the-act.requirement: A frame where a sprite's ink has actually replaced background ink in a shared attribute cell. That needs COLOURED paper behind a moving sprite.
screened_and_rejected: Manic Miner (Bug-Byte 1983) — black paper; sprites stand on the top row of a platform rather than overlapping filled colour
Sabre Wulf (Ultimate 1984) — black arena by design; the colour is in an impassable border
Knight Lore (Ultimate 1984) — one ink per room by design
Auf Wiedersehen Monty (Gremlin 1987) — coloured scenery, but sprites stand on platforms against black paper
Ghosts 'n Goblins (Elite 1986) — filled green ground, but the sprites over it sit in different cell rows
Dizzy (Code Masters 1987) — the right structure, but the snapshot takes no movement input
clash-in-the-act.finding: This is not bad luck in the sample. Every game screened puts its sprites on black paper, which is the dominant design response to the constraint rather than one option among several. The entry lists 'black backgrounds common' as one mitigation among four; the captures suggest it was close to universal. A clash-in-the-act frame therefore needs a game that deliberately did NOT do this, which is the exception.
clash-in-the-act.process_note: Three frames were rejected during this session: two for appearing to show clash and not surviving a close read, one for a misidentified sprite. Captions must describe what is structurally visible (a white sprite on black paper above a green platform) and must not name characters, which proved unreliable at this resolution.
